title: Candidate mosaic — Raphael Zhou (night notes)
content:
Quick context and why I stayed late to scribble this down:

I did a light 1:1 + technical walk with Raphael (resume had strong infra + model-serving ops history). Wanted to capture the pattern fragments that don't fit the panel form — more of a mosaic than a single verdict. These are my raw, unedited notes for handoff and for the committee to pick apart. Treat as 'notes to self' + suggested next steps.

High-level first impressions (gut):
- Confident, calm communicator — explains tradeoffs in simple analogies (cache-as-bridge, batching-as-traffic-control).
- Deep familiarity with inference cost tradeoffs (quantization + caching + sparse batching) — has clear mental models.
- Not strongest on kernel-level pessimal cases (e.g., fused attention fallback paths across mixed-quantized layers) — can reason but slower.
- Good infra hygiene stories (incidents where routing policy prevented SLO regression) — concrete examples.

Behavioral highlights / stories to probe further:
- Story about an incident: multi-tenant model overload, implemented two-layer routing (local fallback + regional spillover). Outcome: 85% reduction in 95th percentile latency spikes in peak window. Questions: what was the rollback plan? how did you measure user-impact (A/B or synthetic)?
- Mentions owning an on-call rotation with a postmortem culture; repeatedly references blameless postmortems and follow-up implementation tickets rather than docs-only.

Technical quick notes (whiteboard sketches in my head translated to text):
- Design idea Raphael described: hierarchical KV cache (per-tenant prefix + shared LRU backplane). He argued it reduced token compute by ~40% on chat-history-heavy workloads.
  - Strength: sensible approach for multi-tenant long-history workloads; operationally lightweight.
  - Risk: eviction policy interactions with pinned tenant caches (doesn't mention QoS isolation).
  - Follow-up: ask him to sketch eviction priority under cross-tenant contention.

- On quantization: prefers per-channel quantization for weights, dynamic quantization for activations in mixed-precision pipelines. Suggests a short-list of models where lower-bit quantization stayed within quality budget.
  - He iterates on evaluation methodology (use domain-specific prompts + holdout prompt set) — good, but confirm reproducibility and calibration step (does he run 10 seeds, or rely on point estimates?).

- Batching strategies: advocates for adaptive batch sizing driven by SLO headroom + real-time latency tail estimates. Conceptually good; needs a concrete admission control algorithm example. Could be a pairing exercise.

Assessment matrix (quick rubric, my shorthand):
- Product sense: 3/4 (ties work to user impact; asks good clarifying questions)
- System depth: 3/4 (strong at architecture & tradeoffs; missing kernel nitty-gritty)
- Debugging / ownership: 4/4 (owned incidents end-to-end, delivered follow-ups)
- Communicating tradeoffs: 4/4 (succinct analogies, can advocate for policy changes)
- Team fit / collaboration: 3.5/4 (high-collab stories; mentions mentoring but limited concrete examples)

Top risks / red flags (things to verify):
- Edge-case device behavior: when we push low-level kernel/quantization bugs, will he iterate quickly on fused-cuda pathways? He seems more infra/systemic than kernel-deep. Not disqualifying but important for senior runtime roles.
- Eviction / QoS nitty-gritty not spelled out — possible mismatch if role requires tight per-tenant SLAs with strict isolation.
- Evaluation rigor: good methodology but unclear on statistical hygiene (run counts, seed variance). If we care about tiny regressions in quality, ensure tests are repeatable.

Suggested next steps (concrete and prioritized):
1) Technical pairing (2 hours): ask Raphael to design an admission controller for batching that preserves 95th percentile latency under sudden bursts. Explicit deliverables: design doc + simulated load run (small harness). Goal: see algorithmic framing and measurable evaluation.
2) Kernel tabletop (30–45m): a focused convo with a senior runtime kernel engineer to surface low-level tradeoffs for mixed-precision attention. Not a grilling session — more of a knowledge probe.
3) Behavioral follow-up (30m): a structured conversation about mentorship and code review examples. Request: bring two PRs he authored and show a before/after with comments.
4) Reference check focused on incident response: confirm ownership + speed of iteration on postmortem action items.

Concrete pairing prompt (short exercise):
- "We have a multi-tenant chat endpoint. Under a traffic spike from Tenant A (long histories), the shared KV cache thrashes and tail latency spikes for all tenants. Design an admission + caching policy that maintains per-tenant 95th percentile latency SLOs and minimizes cost. Sketch the control loop, metrics, and a fail-safe fallback."

What I want to see in that pairing:
- clear definition of metrics (SLO, headroom),
- a short admission control algorithm (token budget vs window vs elastic scaling),
- eviction rules that encode QoS (pinning hot prefixes, tenant-level quotas),
- fallback plan when capacity is exhausted (graceful degradation — degrade to stateless smaller model, or prioritize head tokens),
- simple evaluation plan (synthetic trace + metrics to collect).

Logistics / hiring admin notes:
- Compensation band: Raphael is expecting band 5 / senior principal? He signaled flexibility but wants clarity on scope. Validate with recruiting before offer.
- Timeline: he is 2–3 weeks notice. If we want him, we need to expedite loop scheduling.
- Paperwork: he prefers remote-first but open to quarterly on-site. Flag for People Ops (visa not required).

Questions I still have (for committee):
- Does the role need kernel-level CUDA expertise? If yes, this candidate may need a co-owner or a development plan.
- How important is per-tenant hard isolation vs best-effort QoS? That determines whether his eviction/open-resources approach is acceptable.

Short summary for a vote stub (1–2 lines):
- Raphael Zhou: strong infra-runtime candidate with excellent product sense and incident ownership. Great fit for medium-to-large scale routing/caching/ops problems; may need a kernel-level peer for fused-attention/quantization deep dives. Recommend: advance to pairing + kernel tabletop.

Random scratch ideas to attach to the doc (brain dump):
- Small experiment: run a synthetic workload with tiered tenants (hot long-history vs cold stateless) and measure percent-cost-per-tenant vs latency to quantify benefit of per-tenant KV cache pinning. Could be a quick data point for his design.
- If advanced: ask him to propose a small roadmap for first 90 days (3 bullets per month) to see prioritization.

Notes to self before handing to committee: clean up pairing prompt into a Linear ticket, loop in kernel SME (Satya?) and schedule 90m block. Mark recruiting with his expected comp band and notice period.

End of raw notes.

— Nadia
